learning_outcomes.text: Know how to analyse any thermal engine system in light of the First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics.
Be able to propose improvements in existing thermal engine systems in terms of their characterizing parameters.
Know how to analyse any refrigeration machine and heat pump in light of the First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics as well as propose solutions for better performance.
Be able to analyse non-reactive and reactive gaseous mixtures with emphasis on air conditioning and combustion processes.
Be able to analyze the performance of thermal energy conversion systems.

syllabus_topics: FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS FOR THE ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS ANALYSIS.
Efficiency, work ratio, and specific consumption of steam/gas systems.
THERMODYNAMIC ANALYSIS OF THERMAL ENGINE CYCLES
Carnot, Rankine, Joule-Brayton, and Reciprocating engines cycles.
Analysis of the variables (for engine cycles).
THERMODYNAMIC ANALYSIS OF REFRIGERATING SYSTEMS AND HEAT PUMPS.
Analysis of the variation of the COP of these systems as a function of possible changes that can be implemented in the ideal cycles.
Refrigerant fluids, their classification, and their impact on the environment.
Analysis of variables (for refrigerating systems/heat pumps).
GAS MIXTURES
Mass, molar, and volume fraction of mixtures and their relationship.
Dalton’s, Gibb Dalton’s, and Amagat’s laws.
Thermodynamic properties of gaseous mixtures.
Second Law analysis of mixture processes.
PSYCHROMETRY
Introduction to the theory of psychrometry.
Humid air.
Quantification of water vapor content in humid air.
Psychrometric charts.
Thermodynamic properties of moist air.
Analysis of thermal processes involving humid air and respective energy balances.
REACTIVE MIXTURES
Combustion.
Stoichiometric combustion with excess air, flue analysis, enthalpy of formation, and adiabatic flame temperature.
First and Second Law of Thermodynamics applied to reactive mixtures.
Combustion efficiency.
assessment_rules: Distributed assessment includes a theoretical mini-test (15%) covering the first half of the material and two laboratory works (10%). The final examination period evaluation, accounting for 75% of the grade, consists of a mini-test on Moodle (15% of the total grade) for the second half of the material and a written exam (60% of the total grade) covering all material. Failure to attend theoretical tests, written exams, or laboratory work results in a zero mark. Eligibility requires attendance of at least 75% of the mandatory theoretical-practical classes. Special assessment and classification improvement follow the appeal season rules: a Moodle test (30%), a written exam (60%), and the lab component (10%) which must be obtained beforehand, or results in a 10% loss.
